newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent weakens, other North Sea crudes steady.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent weakens, other North Sea crudes steady.

text.p: North Sea benchmark Dated Brent softened on Monday as sellers struggled to make the transatlantic arbitrage work but other grades were steady ahead of the release of November loading schedules, traders said.
As many as five October Brents were still available despite the sale of one end-month loader at Nov Brent less 10 cents, four cents weaker than the cheapest deal on Friday.

The Brent was bought by a trader who picked up Friday's cargo loading a day earlier, but the fate of the barrels remained unclear as shipping brokers disagreed about whether the provisional fixture of a ULCC for a U.S. trip had failed.
"Brent looks balanced if some moves out of the area but if not we could see a repeat of last month when late September cargoes displaced some early October barrels," said a trader.
Brent CFDs were little moved with the balance of this week a cent off at +29/+32 cents and next week easing to +18/+21 cents.
Other North Sea grades were unchanged from last reported levels with two or three Ekofisk cargoes on offer at about Dated +35 cents and a similar number of Osebergs at Dated +50 cents.
Talk was sparse with buyers waiting to see the details of November loading programmes due out on Tuesday. Flotta and Troll schedules released on Monday showed little change from October.

Nov Brent paper gained 87 cents to $24.85 a barrel by 1730 GMT, propelled higher by renewed fighting in northern Iraq and a weekend refinery fire in the U.S. which showed up the market's vulnerability to low heating oil stocks.
Nigerian differentials were firmer on good demand in northwest Europe, the Mediterranean and the Far East.

In the Med, the last reported Urals deal was last week for a 130,000-tonne cargo loading Oct 18-21 which the seller says was done at Dated -65 cents. Another cargo of Urals loading Oct 20-22 was sold into NWE at Dated -60 cents C&F on Friday.
